q: What is the function of Figure A?
o: Expels unwanted air from inside to the outside of the building.
A commercial and industrial-grade exhaust duct.
Distributes air conditioning to different parts of the building.
Stops or regulates the flow of air in the building.
n: Figure A is a damper, a plate or blade assembly in a duct that stops or regulates the flow of air. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment; SMACNA HVAC Duct Construction Standards.

q: What is the function of Figure B?
n: Figure B is an air diffuser, which spreads supply air into the room in a controlled pattern. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (space air diffusion).

q: What is the function of Figure C?
n: Figure C is a solar roof vent: a roof-mounted exhaust fan driven by its own solar panel that removes hot attic air. Source: Ventilation equipment manufacturer literature.

q: What is the function of Figure D?
n: Figure D is a packaged air-conditioning unit. A packaged unit holds the compressor, condenser, evaporator and fan in one cabinet, so it needs only ducts and power to cool a space. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: What is the function of Figure E?
n: Figure E is a solar water heater, a collector with a tank that uses sunlight to heat water. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (solar energy).

q: Which figure is used for interior room applications?
n: Figure B, the ceiling exhaust fan, ventilates interior rooms such as toilets through a duct. Source: Ventilation equipment manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure can be installed on exterior wall?
n: Figure D, the shuttered wall fan, mounts through an exterior wall and exhausts air directly outdoors. Source: Ventilation equipment manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure do NOT need electricity to run?
n: Figure E, the turbine ventilator, is spun by wind and rising hot air, so it needs no electricity. Source: Ventilation equipment manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure is used for commercial rooftop application?
n: Figure A, the mushroom-type rooftop exhaust fan, is used on commercial roofs to exhaust large volumes of air. Source: AMCA publications; manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure is applicable only for tiny room?
n: Figure C, a small wall fan, only has the capacity for a tiny room such as a toilet. Source: Ventilation equipment manufacturer literature.

q: Which AC component boils the refrigerant, absorbing heat to cool the air?
n: In the evaporator, liquid refrigerant boils at low pressure and absorbs heat from the passing air, cooling it. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (refrigeration cycle).

q: Which control device senses temperature to hold it near the setpoint?
n: A thermostat senses temperature and switches the equipment on and off to keep the space near its setpoint. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (controls).

q: What is the correct amount of refrigerant for an AC to run properly?
n: The operating charge is the correct quantity of refrigerant, specified by the manufacturer, for the system to run efficiently. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Refrigeration; manufacturer service manuals.

q: For maximum efficiency, which components should be located near each other?
n: Locating air handling units near the chiller shortens the chilled-water piping, reducing pumping energy and heat gain, for maximum efficiency. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment (chilled water systems).

q: Which device raises refrigerant pressure in an AC system?
n: The compressor raises the pressure and temperature of the refrigerant vapor so it can reject heat in the condenser. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (vapor compression cycle).

q: What is the minimum clearance from the floor for air-conditioning pipes when crossing a hallway or corridor?
n: Air-conditioning pipes crossing a hallway or corridor must clear the floor by at least 2.30 m, so they do not obstruct people or the required headroom. Source: NBC IRR Rule VIII (ceiling heights and clearances).

q: What is the limitation in the installation of a split-type air conditioner?
o: The refrigerant tubing should not exceed a set length from the condenser to the evaporator
It has a limit of 5 units per building
n: Split-type units have a maximum refrigerant line length (and height difference) between the outdoor condenser and the indoor evaporator, set by the manufacturer, beyond which capacity and oil return suffer. Source: Split-type AC manufacturer installation manuals.

q: Which AC system suits a large, sprawling factory?
n: A large sprawling factory needs a central chilled-water (chiller) system serving AHUs throughout, rather than many small units. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: For a 20 sqm manager's office located in a central core area (center of the floor), which air-conditioning system is most appropriate?
n: In a central core office with no exterior wall for a window or outdoor unit mounting, a ceiling cassette (with remote condensing unit) fits and distributes air evenly in four directions. Source: AC manufacturer application guides; ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: For a high-rise building, where is the best location for a chiller unit?
o: Outside the building near the parking lot
n: In high-rise buildings, heavy chillers are commonly placed in the basement mechanical room, where the slab on grade takes their weight and vibration. Cooling towers go on the roof. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (tall buildings).

q: Where is a cassette-type AC installed?
n: A cassette-type AC is installed flush in the ceiling and discharges air in several directions. Source: AC manufacturer literature.

q: Where is the best place for a cooling tower?
n: Cooling towers must reject heat to open air, so they go on the roof deck where airflow is free and plumes do not affect occupants. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment (cooling towers).

q: If you are installing a centralized air-conditioning system for a building, what additional utility must be provided?
n: A water-cooled centralized system rejects the chiller's heat through condenser water, so a cooling tower must also be provided. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: What carries conditioned air from the air handling unit?
n: Ducts carry conditioned supply air from the AHU to the spaces and return air back. Source: SMACNA HVAC Duct Construction Standards.

q: Where should a window-type air conditioner be installed?
n: A window-type AC is installed high on the wall: cool air sinks, so discharging near the top distributes it better and keeps the unit out of reach. Source: AC manufacturer installation manuals.

q: Air at 100% relative humidity is:
n: Air at 100% relative humidity is saturated: it holds all the water vapor it can at that temperature. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (psychrometrics).

q: Which colorless, odorless gas varies in quantity in air and sets relative humidity?
n: Water vapor is the colorless, odorless gas whose varying amount in air sets the relative humidity. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (psychrometrics).

q: What is the science of lowering the temperature of a space or substance?
n: Refrigeration is the science of lowering the temperature of a space or substance by removing heat. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Refrigeration.

q: A yellow energy guide label on an AC shows a large bold number. What is it?
n: The large bold number on the yellow Philippine energy guide label is the energy efficiency ratio (EER), now CSPF for inverter units: cooling output per unit of power. Source: DOE (Philippines) Philippine Energy Labeling Program.

q: For an AC unit, horsepower describes:
n: For an AC unit, horsepower describes the power of its motor or compressor. Cooling capacity is given in kJ/h, BTU/h or tons. Source: AC manufacturer specifications; ASHRAE terminology.

q: What should a small windowless kitchen or T&B have?
n: A small windowless kitchen or T&B needs a mechanical exhaust fan to remove odors and moisture. Source: NBC IRR Rule VIII (ventilation); ASHRAE 62.2.

q: Which is the best location for a condenser unit?
n: A roof deck gives the condensing unit open air to reject heat, away from occupants and other equipment. Source: AC manufacturer installation manuals.

q: Which ventilation component removes stale or humid air?
n: An exhaust fan removes stale, humid or odorous air from a space. Source: ASHRAE 62.1/62.2 (ventilation).

q: Why must a condenser unit be in a well-ventilated outdoor spot?
n: The condenser rejects the heat removed from the building. If its hot air is trapped, it re-circulates and the unit loses capacity and efficiency, so it needs open, ventilated space. Source: AC manufacturer installation manuals.

q: In ventilation, CFM measures:
n: CFM (cubic feet per minute) measures airflow volume. Airflow in CFM (or L/s) is sized from occupancy, floor area or air changes per hour to meet ventilation requirements. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals.

q: What is installed over an entrance to limit air exchange through the door?
n: An air curtain blows a downward jet of air across an open doorway, limiting the exchange of conditioned and outdoor air, insects and dust. Source: AMCA 220 (air curtain units).

q: Where should the ACCU for a convenience store go?
n: The condensing unit (ACCU) of a store's split system goes outside the store, where it can reject heat to open air. Source: AC manufacturer installation manuals.

q: Which is NOT a standard HVAC component?
n: "FHU" is not a standard HVAC component. ACCUs (air-cooled condensing units), AHUs and condensate drain pipes are. Source: ASHRAE terminology.

q: What is the main function of an AHU?
n: An air handling unit filters, cools or heats and circulates air through the ductwork. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: BTU stands for:
n: BTU = British Thermal Unit, the heat needed to raise 1 lb of water by 1°F (about 1,055 J). Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals.

q: Which is NOT a mode of heat transfer?
n: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation. Evaporation is a phase change that carries latent heat, not one of the three modes. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (heat transfer).

q: What is the method of heat transfer from one room to another?
n: Heat passes from one room to the next through the separating wall or floor mainly by conduction. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (heat transfer).

q: What is installed in ducts where they pass through fire-rated walls?
n: Fire dampers are installed in ducts that pass through fire-rated walls and floors. A fusible link melts in a fire and the damper snaps shut, keeping the rating. Source: NFPA 90A; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019; UL 555.

q: What duct devices near fans, AHUs and dampers absorb or deflect sound to limit its spread?
n: Sound attenuators (duct silencers) placed near fans, AHUs and dampers absorb or deflect noise so it does not travel through the ducts. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (noise and vibration control).

q: Which of the following is NOT a default knob height setting on a shower heater?
n: Shower heater temperature knobs are marked Low, Medium and High. "Standard" is not one of the settings. Source: Shower water heater manufacturer literature.

q: Which part of a split-type AC is outdoors?
n: In a split-type AC, the condenser (with the compressor) is the outdoor unit. The evaporator and blower are indoors. Source: AC manufacturer literature.

q: Which of the following brands does NOT manufacture air conditioners?
n: Carrier, LG and Samsung all make air conditioners. Asahi is known in the Philippines for electric fans and small appliances. Source: Manufacturer company websites.

q: Which part of a split-type AC cools the indoor air?
n: The indoor coil of a split AC is the evaporator, where refrigerant absorbs heat from the room air. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (refrigeration cycle).

q: What is the refrigerant's main job in an AC system?
n: The refrigerant absorbs heat as it evaporates indoors and releases it as it condenses outdoors, carrying heat out of the building. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals.

q: Which AC system suits large commercial spaces?
n: Large commercial spaces are best served by centralized systems (chillers or VRF with AHUs/FCUs). Window and split units suit small rooms. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment.
